purpose: Code-traced B vs C runtime path for the end-to-end decode speed experiment (INFERRED from source; confirm live with call_stats on the pod).
common_path: Int4ProtectedLLM(model, ...) -> vLLM LLM with kv_cache_dtype int4_protected + install_int4_protected_backend swaps each layer .impl to Int4ProtectedAttentionImpl (phase5b_backend_install.py)
decode read -> _read_decode_packed_batched -> get_packed_view -> flash_attn_with_int4_kvcache (EXTERNAL forked vLLM CUDA decode kernel)

B_bf16_protect.write: k_protect_ext bf16; _protect_store = identity; CUDA K-write kernel eligible (fused_decode_write_k.cu) if built, else Python ref

C_int8_protect.write: k_protect_ext uint8; _protect_store = prot_int8_quantize; the CUDA K-write kernel is DISABLED when prot_int8 active (phase5b_4c_paged_writer.py:1003) -> Python quantize chain on WRITE (a PREFILL-side confounder to watch: write_path_fallback / write_path_calls)
C_int8_protect.read: _protect_view_bf16 = prot_int8_dequantize -> materializes a BF16 buffer (k_protect_bf16). CONFIRMED: C materializes bf16 before attention; kernel contract is bf16 either way (phase5b_4c_paged_writer.py:1886).

isolation: Only the protected-sidecar representation differs (bf16 store/passthrough vs uint8 store/dequant). Main INT4 KV, scales, xmins, mask, pages identical.
known_confounders: WRITE path: C disables the CUDA K-write kernel and runs a Python quantize -> may slow PREFILL more than DECODE. Measure prefill/decode separately (this harness does).
enforce_eager=True (CUDA graphs off) matches the validated verify path; CUDA-graph mode is a separate axis.
Both cells MUST show decode_calls_packed>0 and 0 fallbacks, and C must show prot_int8 active==total, else the comparison is not clean.
